newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Caspian Pipeline group details oil volume shares.
newsitem.headline: Caspian Pipeline group details oil volume shares.

text.p: The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) on Tuesday detailed how much oil companies will be able to pump through the planned route once it hits annual capacity of 67 million tonnes (1.34 million barrels per day) in 2014.

Vladimir Stanev, general director of the Russian part of the group known as CPC-Russia, told journalists that Chevron Corp of the United States will get the largest single share at 15 million tonnes a year (300,000 bpd).

CPC-Russia and CPC-Kazakhstan, its Kazakh partner in the project, plan to build a 1,500 km (940 mile) pipeline from the huge Tengiz oil field in Kazakhstan to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet of Novorossiisk.
The $2-billion project is expected to be completed by September 1999. Initial capacity is pegged at 28 million tonnes a year (560,000 bpd), rising to the peak level in four stages.
Stanev said only shareholders would pump into the line throughout the expected 40-year life of the project. "The entire line will be filled by shareholders," he said.
"If there is not enough crude from Kazakhstan (to fill the pipeline), then we will always have enough crude, from, for example, Siberia," he added.
The pipeline will supply oil from Tengiz, other Kazakh fields and from Russia's Siberian deposits, Stanev said. The Russian oil would join the pipeline at Kropotkin, not far from Novorossiisk.
Shareholders are expected to have to pay $25 to transport a tonne of oil from Tengiz to the Black Sea coast.
Russian earnings from taxes and dividends are expected to peak at $900 million a year once full capacity is reached.
CPC officials said that a "quality bank" would be set up, whereby suppliers of oil below the crude standard at Novorossiisk would pay the bank to compensate suppliers of higher quality oil.
